q: The Fredholm alternative for compact operators K: H → H states that for any λ ≠ 0, exactly one of the following holds:
opts: (I − λK)u = f has a unique solution for every f, or the homogeneous equation (I−λK)u = 0 has a non-trivial solution (but not both)
exp: Fredholm alternative: either (I−λK)u = f has a unique solution for all f (when 1/λ is not an eigenvalue of K), or the homogeneous equation has a non-trivial solution (1/λ is an eigenvalue). This dichotomy—analogous to linear algebra—is fundamental to integral equations and spectral theory.
